f1-1.title: What Are C# and .NET? A Plain-English Introduction
f1-1.description: What C# is, what .NET is, and how the language, the CLR runtime and the libraries fit together, plus when C# and .NET are the right choice for a project.

f1-2.title: Install .NET 10 and Set Up Your C# Development Environment
f1-2.description: Install the .NET 10 SDK, choose VS Code or Visual Studio, and see what dotnet run actually does. Covers SDK vs runtime and the layout of a new project.

f1-3.title: Your First C# Program: Create, Build and Run It Step by Step
f1-3.description: Create, build and run your first C# console app with the .NET CLI, then read every line of the code and the .csproj file. Covers dotnet run vs dotnet build.

f2-1.title: C# Variables and Constants: var, const and readonly Explained
f2-1.description: How C# variables and constants store data, when to use var or an explicit type, and the real difference between const and readonly, with simple examples.

f2-2.title: C# Data Types: int, double, decimal, bool, char and More
f2-2.description: A complete tour of C#'s built-in data types with a reference table, plus float vs double vs decimal and when implicit typing with var is the right call.

f2-3.title: C# Strings: Working With Text, StringBuilder and Equality
f2-3.description: How C# strings work and why they never change. Covers StringBuilder, == vs Equals, null vs empty vs whitespace, char vs string, and spans for fast text.

f2-4.title: C# Type Conversion: Casting, Parse, TryParse and Convert
f2-4.description: Convert between types in C# safely: implicit vs explicit casts, Convert vs Parse vs TryParse, the as operator, boxing, and culture-aware number parsing.

f2-5.title: C# Operators Explained: Arithmetic, Comparison and Logical
f2-5.description: Every everyday C# operator with examples: arithmetic, comparison, logical and ternary. Covers = vs ==, && vs &, integer division and operator precedence.

f2-6.title: C# Control Flow: if, switch, for, foreach and while Loops
f2-6.description: Make decisions and repeat work in C# with if/else, switch, for, foreach, while and do-while. Includes break vs continue and switch statement vs expression.

f2-7.title: C# Methods: Parameters, Return Values and Overloading
f2-7.description: Write reusable C# methods: parameters vs arguments, return types and void, static vs instance methods, pass by value vs by reference, and overloading.

f3-1.title: C# Classes and Objects Explained for Beginners
f3-1.description: How C# classes act as blueprints and objects as the real instances, with fields, properties and methods. Covers class vs struct and when to use records.

f3-2.title: C# Fields vs Properties: Getters, Setters and Auto-Properties
f3-2.description: Fields store data and properties control access to it. Learn C# get and set accessors, auto-properties, private setters, and why public fields cause trouble.

f3-3.title: C# Constructors: Default, Chained and Primary Constructors
f3-3.description: How C# constructors set up new objects: default constructors, chaining with this() and base(), and how primary constructors compare to explicit ones.

f3-4.title: C# Static Members: Static Fields, Methods and Constructors
f3-4.description: Static members belong to the type, not to an instance. Learn when to use static fields, methods and constructors in C#, and what static code cannot access.

f3-5.title: C# Access Modifiers: public, private, protected and internal
f3-5.description: Control who can use your C# types and members with public, private, protected and internal, plus protected internal, private protected and the defaults.

f3-6.title: Encapsulation in C#: Hiding Data the Right Way
f3-6.description: Encapsulation in C# explained with examples: why properties beat public fields, how it differs from abstraction, and what an object should keep private.

f3-7.title: C# Value Types vs Reference Types Explained
f3-7.description: The difference between value types and reference types in C#: what gets copied, what gets shared, struct vs class, and what pass by value really means.

f3-8.title: C# Structs: When to Use a Struct Instead of a Class
f3-8.description: What C# structs are, how they differ from classes, and when they make code faster. Clears up myths such as 'structs are always allocated on the stack'.

f3-9.title: C# Enums Explained: Named Constants and [Flags]
f3-9.description: Use C# enums to give names to numbers and make code safer to read. Covers underlying values, the [Flags] attribute and the most common enum misconceptions.

f3-10.title: C# Inheritance for Beginners: Base and Derived Classes
f3-10.description: Build new C# classes on top of existing ones with inheritance. Covers base and derived classes, virtual vs abstract vs override, and base constructors.

f3-11.title: C# Polymorphism for Beginners: virtual and override
f3-11.description: Polymorphism lets C# treat different objects through one base type or interface. Learn virtual, override and abstract, and when polymorphism really helps.

f3-12.title: C# Method Overloading vs Overriding: The Difference
f3-12.description: Overloading gives one method name several parameter lists. Overriding lets a derived class replace a base method. See both in C# with clear examples.

f3-13.title: C# Interfaces for Beginners: Contracts Explained
f3-13.description: A C# interface is a contract a class promises to fulfil. Learn how to declare and implement interfaces, and when to choose an interface or an abstract class.

f3-14.title: Composition vs Inheritance in C#: When to Use Each
f3-14.description: 'Is-a' vs 'has-a': why C# developers often prefer composition over inheritance, the problems deep hierarchies cause, and how to choose between them.

f4-1.title: C# Arrays: Declare, Initialize and Loop Through Arrays
f4-1.description: C# arrays hold a fixed number of same-typed values with instant index access. Learn to create and use them, and how an array differs from a List<T>.

f4-2.title: C# Multidimensional Arrays: 2D Grids With int[,]
f4-2.description: Store grids of data with C# multidimensional arrays. Learn the int[,] syntax, GetLength vs Length, and how rectangular arrays differ from jagged arrays.

f4-3.title: C# Jagged Arrays: Arrays of Arrays Explained
f4-3.description: A jagged array in C# is an array of arrays where each row can have its own length. Learn the syntax, how it differs from int[,], and when to use one.

f4-4.title: C# List<T> Explained: The Everyday Resizable Collection
f4-4.description: List<T> is the C# collection you will use most. Learn how it grows, how to add and remove items, and the difference between Count, Length and Capacity.

f4-5.title: C# Dictionary<TKey,TValue>: Key/Value Lookups Explained
f4-5.description: Store key/value pairs in a C# Dictionary and find values almost instantly. Covers TryGetValue vs the indexer, ordering, and Dictionary vs a list of pairs.

f4-6.title: C# HashSet<T>: Store Unique Values With Fast Lookups
f4-6.description: A HashSet in C# keeps only unique values with dictionary-speed lookups. Learn when to use HashSet<T> instead of a List or a Dictionary, with examples.

f4-7.title: C# Stack vs Queue: LIFO and FIFO Collections Explained
f4-7.description: Stack<T> gives back the last item added and Queue<T> the first. Learn Push, Pop, Enqueue and Dequeue in C#, and when each of the two collections fits.

f4-8.title: C# Collection Interfaces: IEnumerable, ICollection, IList
f4-8.description: The contracts every C# collection shares: IEnumerable<T>, ICollection<T>, IList<T> and the read-only versions, and which one to use as a parameter type.

f4-9.title: IEnumerable<T> in C#: How foreach Really Works
f4-9.description: IEnumerable<T> is the one promise every C# collection makes. Learn how foreach uses it, how it differs from IEnumerator<T>, and why it has no Count.

f5-1.title: C# Exception Handling: try, catch and finally Explained
f5-1.description: Handle errors in C# with try, catch and finally. Learn the exception hierarchy, multiple catch blocks, and why exceptions beat easily ignored error codes.

f5-2.title: C# Custom Exceptions: Creating and Throwing Errors
f5-2.description: Create your own exception types in C#, throw them correctly, and avoid the throw ex stack-trace trap. Also covers exception filters with the when keyword.

f5-3.title: C# File and Directory Operations: Read and Write Files
f5-3.description: Read, write and manage files and folders in C# with the File and Directory classes, and learn why async I/O matters once your code touches the disk.

f5-4.title: C# File Paths: Path.Combine and Cross-Platform Paths
f5-4.description: Build file paths that work on Windows, Linux and macOS with Path.Combine and friends, and learn what a relative path is actually relative to in .NET.

f5-5.title: C# Streams Explained: FileStream, StreamReader and using
f5-5.description: A stream is data flowing in or out, not a fixed pile. Learn FileStream vs StreamReader in C# and why using statements matter for releasing resources.

f5-6.title: C# DateTime vs DateTimeOffset: Which One Should You Use?
f5-6.description: DateTime vs DateTimeOffset in C#: why DateTime.Kind can't be trusted, why you should store UTC, and how DateTimeOffset records exactly when something happened.

f5-7.title: C# Time Zones: Store UTC and Convert With TimeZoneInfo
f5-7.description: Handle time zones correctly in .NET: store UTC, convert to local time only for display with TimeZoneInfo, and avoid fixed offsets that break with DST.

f5-8.title: Working With JSON in C#: System.Text.Json Basics
f5-8.description: Serialize and deserialize JSON in C# with System.Text.Json, set the common options, and see why JSON became the shared language of web APIs.

f5-9.title: C# Serialization Explained: Turning Objects Into Data
f5-9.description: What serialization means in .NET, how JSON relates to it, which other formats such as XML exist, and how to choose a format for your C# application.

f6-1.title: C# Nullable Reference Types: Catch Null Bugs at Compile Time
f6-1.description: Turn on nullable reference types in C# and let the compiler warn about null bugs before runtime. Covers string? vs string and nullable value types.

f6-2.title: C# Null Handling: ?., ??, ??= and the ! Operator
f6-2.description: Handle null cleanly in C# with the null-conditional ?. operator and null-coalescing ?? and ??=, and learn why the null-forgiving ! operator checks nothing.

f6-3.title: C# Pattern Matching Explained With Examples
f6-3.description: Use C# pattern matching to test a value's type and shape in one expression: type, property, relational and logical patterns with is and switch.

f6-4.title: C# Records Explained: record vs class and the with Expression
f6-4.description: C# records compare by value, not by reference. Learn record vs class, how with creates modified copies, and why records are not automatically immutable.

f6-5.title: C# Tuples and Deconstruction: Return Multiple Values
f6-5.description: Return several values from a C# method with tuples, name the elements, and unpack them with deconstruction. Covers ValueTuple vs the old System.Tuple.

f6-6.title: C# Switch Expressions: Modern switch With Examples
f6-6.description: Switch expressions in C# produce a value instead of running statements. Learn the syntax, why the first matching arm wins, and exhaustiveness warnings.

f6-7.title: C# Collection Expressions: The [ ] Syntax and Spread ..
f6-7.description: Create arrays, lists and spans with one [ ] syntax in modern C#. Learn how collection expressions pick a target type and how the .. spread element works.

f6-8.title: C# required Members: Mandatory Properties Explained
f6-8.description: The C# required modifier makes callers set key properties in an object initializer. Learn how it works with init, constructors and nullable types.

f6-9.title: C# Primary Constructors for Classes and Structs
f6-9.description: Primary constructors put constructor parameters on the type declaration in C# 12 and later. Learn how they work and how they differ from positional records.

f7-1.title: Debugging C# Code: Breakpoints, Step Into and Step Over
f7-1.description: Stop guessing and start inspecting. Learn to debug C# with breakpoints, Step Into vs Step Over, and variable inspection instead of print statements.

f7-2.title: How to Read a C# Stack Trace and Find the Bug Fast
f7-2.description: A .NET stack trace is a map to the bug. Learn to read it line by line, why the top line isn't always the cause, and why throw; beats throw ex;.

f7-3.title: Writing Clean C# Code: Practical Rules for Beginners
f7-3.description: Write C# that other people can read: clear names, small methods and simple logic. Learn why clean does not mean clever, and short does not mean clear.

f7-4.title: C# Naming Conventions: PascalCase, camelCase and _fields
f7-4.description: The standard .NET naming conventions in one table: PascalCase vs camelCase, the underscore prefix for private fields, and why Hungarian notation is out.

f7-5.title: Common C# Beginner Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
f7-5.description: The mistakes almost every new C# developer makes, from value vs reference confusion and == vs Equals to a missing override and catching exceptions too broadly.

f7-6.title: C# Beginner Project: Build an Expense Tracker Console App
f7-6.description: Build a complete C# console app that tracks expenses, using classes, collections, file storage and exception handling together. Full solution included.

f7-7.title: C# OOP Project: Build an Employee Payroll System
f7-7.description: Practise C# inheritance and polymorphism by building a payroll system with different employee types and one shared contract. Full solution included.

f7-8.title: C# Fundamentals Challenge: Test What You've Learned
f7-8.description: Challenges covering the whole C# Foundations tier, from types and control flow to OOP and collections. Find out how much stuck before moving on.

i1-1.title: Object-Oriented Programming in C#: Beyond the Basics
i1-1.description: Revisit the four OOP pillars in C# with a working developer's eye: what changes when you build real systems with encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism.

i1-2.title: Encapsulation in Real C# Applications: Rich Domain Models
i1-2.description: Real encapsulation protects the rules your objects must never break. Learn rich vs anemic domain models in C#, and how to encapsulate a collection safely.

i1-3.title: C# Inheritance in Depth: The Fragile Base Class Problem
i1-3.description: What happens to C# inheritance in large codebases: the fragile base class problem, virtual, override and sealed override, and constructor chaining with base.

i1-4.title: Composition in C#: Building Flexible, Testable Services
i1-4.description: Use composition as the structure of real C# services: compose small parts, apply the strategy shape, and build a notification service from components.

i1-5.title: Polymorphism in Practice: Polymorphic Collections in C#
i1-5.description: Put polymorphism to work in C#: polymorphic collections, the Liskov Substitution Principle, and one reporting engine built two ways to compare designs.

i1-6.title: C# Abstract Classes: When to Use Them vs Interfaces
i1-6.description: An abstract class in C# shares implementation and enforces a contract. Learn abstract vs virtual methods and when to choose an abstract class or interface.

i1-7.title: C# sealed Classes and Members: When and Why to Seal
i1-7.description: Use the C# sealed keyword to stop a class being inherited or a member being overridden further. Learn sealed override and when sealing is the right call.

i1-8.title: C# Interfaces in Depth: Default Methods, DI and Testing
i1-8.description: Go deeper with C# interfaces: default interface methods, interfaces as team boundaries, and designing interfaces for dependency injection and unit tests.

i1-9.title: Implementing Multiple Interfaces in C#
i1-9.description: One C# class can implement several interfaces to combine capabilities. Learn how to resolve member name conflicts and how this differs from inheritance.

i1-10.title: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) in C# With Examples
i1-10.description: The I in SOLID: no class should depend on methods it doesn't use. See how fat C# interfaces hurt, and split a bloated IRepository step by step.

i1-11.title: C# Explicit Interface Implementation Explained
i1-11.description: Use explicit interface implementation in C# when two interfaces clash or a member should only be reachable through the interface. Syntax and examples.

i1-12.title: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) in C# With Examples
i1-12.description: The D in SOLID explained in C#: depend on abstractions, not concrete classes. Learn what gets inverted and apply DIP step by step to an order service.

i2-1.title: C# Generics Explained: Type-Safe Reusable Code
i2-1.description: Generics let one piece of C# code work with any type while keeping type safety. Learn the problem generics solve, what T means, and why they beat object.

i2-2.title: C# Generic Classes: Writing Your Own Generic Types
i2-2.description: Write your own generic classes in C#: one or more type parameters, how they flow through members, and using primary constructors with generic types.

i2-3.title: C# Generic Methods: Type Parameters on a Single Method
i2-3.description: A C# method can be generic on its own, even inside a non-generic class. Learn the syntax, type inference, and when to pass explicit type arguments.

i2-4.title: C# Generic Constraints: Telling the Compiler What T Can Do
i2-4.description: Unconstrained T can do almost nothing. Learn how C# generic constraints unlock members on T, what they restrict, and why compiling for int proves little.

i2-5.title: C# where Constraints: class, struct, new() and notnull
i2-5.description: A practical guide to C# where constraints: class, struct, new(), notnull, base classes and interfaces, and how to pick exactly the one your code needs.

i2-6.title: C# Covariance and Contravariance: in and out Explained
i2-6.description: Why a List<Dog> is not a List<Animal> but an IEnumerable<Dog> is an IEnumerable<Animal>. Learn C# generic variance with the in and out keywords.

i2-7.title: C# Generic Collections: List, Dictionary, SortedList and More
i2-7.description: A guided tour of .NET's generic collections: List<T>, Dictionary, HashSet, SortedList vs SortedDictionary, LinkedList<T>, and how to choose one.

i2-8.title: How a C# Dictionary Works Internally: Hashing and Buckets
i2-8.description: Why a .NET Dictionary lookup is O(1): hash codes, buckets and collisions explained step by step, and why buckets don't preserve insertion order.

i2-9.title: C# Equals and GetHashCode: Equality and Hashing Explained
i2-9.description: Equals and GetHashCode form one contract in C#. Learn ReferenceEquals vs Equals vs ==, why equal hashes don't mean equal objects, and how to override both.

i2-10.title: C# IComparable<T>: Sorting Your Own Types
i2-10.description: Teach List<T>.Sort() and Array.Sort() how to order your own C# types by implementing IComparable<T> and CompareTo, with examples and common pitfalls.

i2-11.title: C# IEquatable<T>: Fast, Type-Safe Equality for Your Types
i2-11.description: Implement IEquatable<T> in C# for type-safe equality without boxing structs. Learn how Equals(T) relates to Equals(object) and why GetHashCode still matters.

i2-12.title: Build a Custom Collection in C# With IEnumerable<T>
i2-12.description: Build your own C# collection from scratch: implement IEnumerable<T> with yield return, and decide when implementing ICollection<T> is worth the effort.

i3-1.title: C# Delegates Explained: Methods as Variables
i3-1.description: A C# delegate is a variable that holds a method, so behaviour can be passed around like data. Learn how to declare, assign and invoke delegates.

i3-2.title: C# Custom and Multicast Delegates Explained
i3-2.description: Declare your own delegate types in C# and use multicast delegates to call a whole list of methods from one trigger, with += and -= explained precisely.

i3-3.title: C# Action Delegate: Action, Action<T> and When to Use It
i3-3.description: Action is the ready-made C# delegate for methods that return nothing. Learn Action and Action<T> with examples, and why you rarely need custom void delegates.

i3-4.title: C# Func Delegate: Func<T, TResult> Explained With Examples
i3-4.description: Func is the built-in C# delegate for methods that return a value, and the type behind most LINQ methods. Learn which type parameter is the return type.

i3-5.title: C# Predicate<T> vs Func<T, bool>: What's the Difference?
i3-5.description: Predicate<T> is a named C# delegate for testing a condition. Learn how it relates to Func<T, bool>, why both exist, and why you can't swap them freely.

i3-6.title: C# Lambda Expressions: The => Syntax Explained
i3-6.description: A lambda in C# is a nameless method written inline with =>. Learn expression and statement lambdas, how they become delegates, and where you use them daily.

i3-7.title: C# Closures Explained: Captured Variables and Loop Traps
i3-7.description: When a C# lambda captures an outside variable, it captures the variable itself, not a copy. Learn how closures work and avoid the classic loop variable trap.

i3-8.title: C# Local Functions vs Lambdas: When to Use Each
i3-8.description: Local functions are named helpers inside a C# method. Learn how they differ from lambdas, why they suit recursion, and how they avoid delegate overhead.

i3-9.title: Higher-Order Functions in C# With Func and Action
i3-9.description: Higher-order functions take or return other functions. See how C# uses Func and Action to separate what varies from what stays the same, with examples.

i3-10.title: C# Events Explained: The event Keyword and Subscribers
i3-10.description: The C# event keyword wraps a delegate so subscribers can only add or remove themselves. Learn how events work and why a raw delegate field is unsafe.

i3-11.title: C# Event Pattern: EventHandler, EventArgs and Memory Leaks
i3-11.description: The standard .NET event pattern: EventHandler<T>, EventArgs, a protected raiser method, thread-safe raising, and the memory leak caused by not unsubscribing.

i3-12.title: Event-Driven Design in C#: Decoupling With Events
i3-12.description: Use C# events to decouple an application: publish a fact and let other components react, without the publisher ever knowing who is listening.

i4-1.title: C# LINQ Tutorial for Beginners: Introduction to LINQ
i4-1.description: LINQ lets you query data in C# by saying what you want instead of writing loops. A beginner-friendly introduction to LINQ with before-and-after examples.

i4-2.title: IEnumerable vs IQueryable in C#: The Key Difference
i4-2.description: IEnumerable<T> runs a LINQ query in memory, while IQueryable<T> translates it to run somewhere else, such as a database. Learn when each one is used.

i4-3.title: LINQ Where in C#: Filtering Collections With Examples
i4-3.description: Filter C# collections with LINQ's Where, filter by type with OfType<T>, and use index-aware filtering. Also covers OfType vs Cast and chained Where calls.

i4-4.title: LINQ Select and SelectMany in C#: Projection Explained
i4-4.description: Reshape data with LINQ projection in C#: Select to transform each item and SelectMany to flatten nested collections into one sequence, with examples.

i4-5.title: LINQ OrderBy and ThenBy in C#: Sorting Explained
i4-5.description: Sort sequences with LINQ's OrderBy, OrderByDescending and ThenBy in C#. Learn why OrderBy returns a new sequence and how it differs from List<T>.Sort().

i4-6.title: LINQ GroupBy in C#: Grouping Data With Examples
i4-6.description: Group items by key with LINQ GroupBy in C#. Learn IGrouping<TKey,TElement>, element and result selectors, and why grouping does not sort your data.

i4-7.title: LINQ Join and GroupJoin in C#: Combining Collections
i4-7.description: Combine two collections on a shared key with LINQ Join, keep unmatched items with GroupJoin, and learn why LINQ's Join is always an equi-join.

i4-8.title: LINQ Aggregation in C#: Count, Sum, Average, Min, Max
i4-8.description: Collapse a sequence to one value with LINQ's Count, Sum, Average, Min, Max and Aggregate in C#, and see how each one behaves on an empty sequence.

i4-9.title: LINQ Deferred Execution in C#: When Queries Actually Run
i4-9.description: A LINQ query in C# doesn't run when you write it. Learn deferred execution, why queries re-run on every enumeration, and how captured variables surprise you.

i4-10.title: LINQ Immediate Execution: ToList, ToArray and ToDictionary
i4-10.description: Force a LINQ query to run now with ToList, ToArray, ToDictionary and ToHashSet. Learn when immediate execution is the right choice, and ToList vs ToArray.

i4-11.title: LINQ Query Syntax in C#: from, where, select and let
i4-11.description: Write LINQ in C# with SQL-like query syntax using from, where, select and let. Learn what query syntax can't express and why it is not actually SQL.

i4-12.title: LINQ Method Syntax in C#: Chaining Where, Select and More
i4-12.description: Method syntax is what C# compiles LINQ query syntax into. Learn to build readable LINQ method chains step by step, and when to prefer each style.

i4-13.title: Write Custom LINQ Extension Methods in C#
i4-13.description: Where and Select are just extension methods. Learn to write your own custom LINQ operators in C# and chain them into real queries like the built-in ones.

i4-14.title: LINQ Performance in C#: Common Pitfalls and Fixes
i4-14.description: What LINQ really costs in C#: multiple enumeration, Count() vs Count, needless ToList calls mid-chain and operator order, with a fix for each pitfall.

i5-1.title: Dependency Injection in .NET: A Beginner-Friendly Guide
i5-1.description: Dependency injection in .NET explained simply: why classes shouldn't build their own dependencies, and how the built-in container supplies them instead.

i5-2.title: Service Lifetimes in .NET DI: Singleton, Scoped, Transient
i5-2.description: Choose the right .NET dependency injection lifetime: Singleton, Scoped or Transient. Learn how each one reuses objects and the mistakes to avoid.

i5-3.title: Configuration in .NET: appsettings.json and IConfiguration
i5-3.description: Load settings in .NET from appsettings.json, environment variables and other sources with IConfiguration, and learn how layered overrides really work.

i5-4.title: Options Pattern in .NET: IOptions, IOptionsSnapshot, Monitor
i5-4.description: Bind configuration to typed classes with the .NET Options pattern. Learn IOptions vs IOptionsSnapshot vs IOptionsMonitor and how to validate settings.

i5-5.title: Logging in .NET: ILogger and Structured Logging Explained
i5-5.description: Log the right way in .NET with ILogger and message templates. Learn why structured logs with named placeholders beat string interpolation and free text.

i5-6.title: Environment-Based Configuration in ASP.NET Core and .NET
i5-6.description: Run the same .NET build differently in Development, Staging and Production. Learn how the environment name selects appsettings files and settings.

i5-7.title: HttpClient in .NET: IHttpClientFactory and Best Practices
i5-7.description: Why new HttpClient() causes problems in .NET, and how IHttpClientFactory shares connections safely. Also clears up when you should and shouldn't dispose it.

i5-8.title: Calling JSON APIs in C# With HttpClient and GetFromJsonAsync
i5-8.description: Call JSON web APIs from C# by combining HttpClient with System.Text.Json helpers like GetFromJsonAsync, and learn to check status codes, not just exceptions.

i5-9.title: REST API Fundamentals for .NET Developers
i5-9.description: The conventions behind REST APIs: resources, HTTP verbs and their meaning, and status codes, explained for .NET developers with practical examples.

i5-10.title: OpenAPI in ASP.NET Core: Generate API Documentation
i5-10.description: Generate OpenAPI documentation from your ASP.NET Core code so it never goes stale, with a guided tour of how to read an OpenAPI document.

i6-1.title: ADO.NET Tutorial: Connections, Commands and Data Readers
i6-1.description: ADO.NET is the layer under every .NET database library. Learn connections, commands and data readers, and why ADO.NET is still relevant today.

i6-2.title: ADO.NET Database Connections and Connection Pooling
i6-2.description: Why opening a SQL connection per query is fine in .NET: connection pooling explained, why to always use using, and the pool settings worth knowing.

i6-3.title: ADO.NET Commands: ExecuteReader, ExecuteScalar, NonQuery
i6-3.description: Run SQL from C# with the right ADO.NET command method: ExecuteReader for rows, ExecuteScalar for a single value, and ExecuteNonQuery for changes.

i6-4.title: SQL Parameters in C#: Prevent SQL Injection in ADO.NET
i6-4.description: Stop SQL injection in C# with parameterized queries. See how string-built SQL lets data rewrite your query, and how ADO.NET parameters keep them apart.

i6-5.title: Database Transactions in C#: ACID and ADO.NET Explained
i6-5.description: Group related SQL statements into one atomic unit with ADO.NET transactions in C#. Learn the ACID guarantees, commit and rollback, with examples.

i6-6.title: Entity Framework Core Tutorial: Getting Started With EF Core
i6-6.description: Get started with Entity Framework Core: the problem an ORM solves, how to install and set up EF Core in a .NET project, and your first queries and saves.

i6-7.title: EF Core DbContext Explained: DbSet, Lifetime and Tracking
i6-7.description: Everything in EF Core runs through DbContext. Learn DbSet<T>, change tracking, how to register DbContext with dependency injection, and its lifetime.

i6-8.title: EF Core Entities: Conventions, Data Annotations, Fluent API
i6-8.description: How EF Core maps C# classes to tables by convention, and how to override the defaults with data annotations or the Fluent API, with examples.

i6-9.title: EF Core Relationships: One-to-Many and Navigation Properties
i6-9.description: Model related tables in EF Core with navigation properties and foreign keys. Covers one-to-many relationships with customers, orders and order lines.

i6-10.title: EF Core Migrations Tutorial: dotnet ef Commands Explained
i6-10.description: Keep your database schema in sync with EF Core migrations. Learn the dotnet ef CLI commands step by step, and why manually altered schemas drift.

i6-11.title: LINQ With EF Core: How Your Queries Become SQL
i6-11.description: EF Core translates your C# LINQ into SQL that runs in the database. Learn how translation works and the classic gotcha that pulls whole tables into memory.

i6-12.title: EF Core AsNoTracking vs Tracking Queries Explained
i6-12.description: EF Core tracks every entity a query returns by default. Learn when AsNoTracking speeds up read-only queries, and what no-tracking does and doesn't mean.

i6-13.title: EF Core Transactions and Concurrency Tokens Explained
i6-13.description: Make multi-step EF Core saves atomic with explicit transactions, and detect conflicting edits to the same row with a concurrency token.

i6-14.title: Repository Pattern With EF Core: Do You Really Need It?
i6-14.description: Should you wrap EF Core's DbContext in a repository? The honest case for and against the repository pattern in .NET, and how to decide for your project.

i7-1.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Programming in C#
i7-1.description: Why blocking threads wastes resources and how asynchronous C# code frees them. Learn what async really means and how it differs from multithreading.

i7-2.title: Task and Task<T> in C#: Async Basics Explained
i7-2.description: A Task in C# is a handle for work that may not be finished yet. Learn Task vs Task<T>, how to get a result, and why a Task does not mean a new thread.

i7-3.title: C# async and await Explained Step by Step
i7-3.description: What async and await really do in C#: pause, free the thread, and resume when the result is ready. Learn the syntax, and why to go async all the way.

i7-4.title: CancellationToken in C#: Cancel Async Operations Safely
i7-4.description: Cancellation in .NET is cooperative. Learn to pass a CancellationToken, check it in async C# code, and why Cancel() never stops work immediately.

i7-5.title: Task.WhenAll in C#: Run Async Tasks Concurrently
i7-5.description: Run independent async operations at the same time with Task.WhenAll in C#, and learn how it collects every exception when more than one task fails.

i7-6.title: Task.WhenAny in C#: Act on the First Task to Finish
i7-6.description: Use Task.WhenAny in C# to react to whichever task finishes first, and remember that WhenAny never cancels the tasks that lose the race.

i7-7.title: Exception Handling in Async C#: try/catch With await
i7-7.description: How exceptions flow through async C# code: they are captured on the Task and rethrown at await. Covers try/catch around await and unobserved exceptions.

i7-8.title: Async Streams in C#: IAsyncEnumerable and await foreach
i7-8.description: Async streams let C# consume values that arrive over time. Learn IAsyncEnumerable<T> and await foreach, and when a stream beats returning a whole list.

i7-9.title: IAsyncEnumerable<T> in C#: Write Async Iterators
i7-9.description: Write your own async iterators in C# by combining yield return with await, including streaming paginated API results as each page arrives.

i7-10.title: Common Async/Await Mistakes in C# and How to Fix Them
i7-10.description: Five async/await mistakes that compile fine but cause real bugs in C#, from async void to blocking on async code, with the fix for each one.

i8-1.title: Build a REST API in ASP.NET Core: Step-by-Step Project
i8-1.description: Build a working REST API with ASP.NET Core using dependency injection, configuration and logging. A step-by-step project with a complete solution.

i8-2.title: Employee Management API Project With EF Core and Async
i8-2.description: Build an employee management API in .NET with EF Core persistence, real relationships, LINQ queries and async all the way down. Full solution included.

i8-3.title: EF Core Database Project: Schema, Relationships and LINQ
i8-3.description: Practise EF Core on a real schema with relationships and LINQ queries that have to perform. A step-by-step .NET project with a complete solution.

i8-4.title: Notification Service Project in C#: Interfaces and Events
i8-4.description: Build a pluggable notification service in C# using interfaces for swappable senders and events for decoupled communication. Complete solution included.

i8-5.title: Background Service in .NET: BackgroundService and Channels
i8-5.description: Build a .NET background processing service with IHostedService, BackgroundService and Channel<T> to move work out of HTTP requests. Full solution.

i8-6.title: Intermediate C# Challenge: Test Your .NET Skills
i8-6.description: Challenges covering the whole C# In Practice tier: OOP, generics, delegates, LINQ, dependency injection, EF Core and async. Find out what stuck.

a1-1.title: How C# Code Executes: IL, JIT, ReadyToRun and Native AOT
a1-1.description: Follow C# from source code to machine code: compilation to IL, JIT compilation at runtime, and how ReadyToRun and Native AOT change the picture.

a1-2.title: CLR Internals: How the .NET Runtime Works
a1-2.description: What the Common Language Runtime does underneath your C# code: garbage collection, exceptions, generics and type safety, and how the CLR differs from .NET.

a1-3.title: .NET JIT Compiler Explained: How Tiered Compilation Works
a1-3.description: How the .NET JIT decides what to optimize: tier 0 and tier 1 compilation, why it bets on hot methods, and what that means for startup and throughput.

a1-4.title: .NET Garbage Collection Explained: How the GC Works
a1-4.description: How the .NET garbage collector frees memory you never release yourself: reachability, why objects aren't freed instantly, and why .NET skips reference counting.

a1-5.title: .NET Generational GC: Gen 0, Gen 1, Gen 2 and the LOH
a1-5.description: Most objects die young, and the .NET GC is built around that. Learn generations 0, 1 and 2, the Large Object Heap, and Server vs Workstation GC.

a1-6.title: Memory Allocation in .NET: How the Managed Heap Works
a1-6.description: Allocating in .NET is cheap but not free. Learn bump-pointer allocation on the managed heap, what allocations really cost, and when reducing them pays off.

a1-7.title: Stack vs Heap in C#: Where Values Really Live
a1-7.description: 'Value types live on the stack' is an oversimplification. Learn the precise C# rule for stack and heap allocation, walked through one method call at a time.

a1-8.title: Boxing and Unboxing in C#: Hidden Costs Explained
a1-8.description: Boxing wraps a C# value type in a heap object. Learn exactly when it happens, what it costs, and how ArrayList vs List<T> shows the difference.

a1-9.title: C# Value Types vs Reference Types in Depth: readonly struct
a1-9.description: Beyond the basics: what actually gets copied in C#, why mutable structs plus copying is a trap, and how readonly struct makes value types safe.

a1-10.title: C# Records vs Record Structs: Immutability Explained
a1-10.description: C# record class vs record struct: why a record struct is mutable by default, how readonly record struct changes that, and when to choose each one.

a1-11.title: C# Pattern Matching in Depth: List, Slice and Positional
a1-11.description: Advanced C# pattern matching: list patterns, slice patterns with .., and positional patterns using Deconstruct, plus the rules that trip people up.

a1-12.title: Advanced C# Generics: How the CLR Shares Generic Code
a1-12.description: How .NET compiles generics: shared code for reference types, specialised code for value types, and why C# generics are not erased like Java generics.

a1-13.title: Variance in C# and .NET: Array Covariance and Generic Rules
a1-13.description: Why string[] can pose as object[] in .NET and fail at runtime, and how generic variance with in and out avoids that by checking positions at compile time.

a1-14.title: Reflection in C#: Inspect Types and Members at Runtime
a1-14.description: Use reflection in C# to read types, members and attributes at runtime, the way DI containers and serializers do, and learn its real costs and limits.

a1-15.title: C# Attributes Explained: Custom Attributes and Metadata
a1-15.description: C# attributes are pure metadata that never run on their own. Learn built-in attributes like [Obsolete], create custom ones, and read them with reflection.

a1-16.title: C# Source Generators: Introduction and First Example
a1-16.description: Source generators write C# code at compile time instead of using reflection at runtime. Learn what they are, how they work, and what they can't do.

a2-1.title: Advanced C# Delegates: Multicast, Invocation Lists, Gotchas
a2-1.description: Open up C# delegates: the class hierarchy underneath, invocation lists, and the gotchas with exceptions and return values in multicast delegates.

a2-2.title: Action, Func and Predicate in Depth: Real Declarations
a2-2.description: Read the real .NET declarations of Action, Func and Predicate, see why the family has a fixed size, and what each delegate type actually costs.

a2-3.title: C# Expression Trees Explained: Code as Data
a2-3.description: A lambda compiled to Expression<TDelegate> is a data structure you can read. Learn how expression trees let libraries translate C# into other languages.

a2-4.title: How C# Lambdas Compile: Allocations and Closures Inside
a2-4.description: Does this lambda allocate? Learn the strategies the C# compiler uses to compile lambdas, from cached delegates to closure classes, and what each one costs.

a2-5.title: C# Closures Under the Hood: Captured State and Leaks
a2-5.description: See what a C# closure compiles to: captured variables promoted to a heap object, and how that can keep objects alive and quietly cause a memory leak.

a2-6.title: Advanced C# Events: Custom add/remove and Event Leaks
a2-6.description: Write custom add and remove accessors for C# events, control how subscribers are stored, and fix the memory leak that long-lived event sources cause.

a2-7.title: Event Aggregator Pattern in C#: Decoupled Messaging
a2-7.description: Decouple publishers and subscribers completely with an event aggregator in C#: one shared hub known to everyone, shown with an order fulfilment example.

a2-8.title: C# Extension Methods Explained: How LINQ Is Built
a2-8.description: Extension methods let you add methods to types you don't own. Learn how C# resolves them, how the this parameter works, and why all of LINQ uses them.

a2-9.title: C# 14 Extension Members: Extension Properties Preview
a2-9.description: C# 14 extends extension methods to extension properties and static members using the new extension block syntax. A first look at how the feature works.

a3-1.title: IEnumerable<T> Internals: How yield return Compiles
a3-1.description: Every C# iterator with yield return becomes a hidden state machine class. Learn the exact interface shapes and read the generated code line by line.

a3-2.title: IQueryable<T> Explained: Queryable vs Enumerable in LINQ
a3-2.description: Why Where means two different things in C#: Enumerable methods take delegates, Queryable methods take expression trees. Learn how IQueryable<T> works.

a3-3.title: Reading Expression Trees in C#: ExpressionVisitor Explained
a3-3.description: Learn how a LINQ provider reads an expression tree in C#, using ExpressionVisitor to walk and rewrite trees, with a minimal pretty-printer example.

a3-4.title: LINQ Deferred Execution in Depth: Objects vs Queryables
a3-4.description: Deferred execution works through two different mechanisms in .NET: iterator state machines in LINQ to Objects and expression trees in IQueryable providers.

a3-5.title: LINQ Performance Internals: What LINQ Costs in .NET
a3-5.description: What LINQ really costs at the CLR level: an iterator object per operator, pattern-based foreach and struct enumerators, plus a boxing trap many miss.

a3-6.title: Custom LINQ Operators in C#: Design Them Like the BCL
a3-6.description: Design production-quality custom LINQ operators in C#: argument validation, staying lazy on infinite sources, and the honest limits with IQueryable.

a3-7.title: LINQ to Objects Explained: One Query Syntax, Many Sources
a3-7.description: LINQ to Objects is the LINQ you have been writing all along. Learn its name, how it works, and where it sits in the family of LINQ providers.

a3-8.title: LINQ to EF Core: How Queries Are Translated to SQL
a3-8.description: How EF Core's provider turns C# LINQ into SQL, which expressions translate and which don't, and exactly where the translation machinery runs out.

a3-9.title: How LINQ Translates to SQL: Where, OrderBy, GroupBy, Join
a3-9.description: See the SQL behind each LINQ operator in EF Core: Where to WHERE, OrderBy to ORDER BY, Select to columns, GroupBy and more, plus why collation matters.

a3-10.title: Avoiding LINQ Performance Traps in Production .NET
a3-10.description: LINQ mistakes that compile, pass code review, and slow production down, from multiple enumeration onwards, each with what really happens and the fix.

a4-1.title: How async/await Works Internally: The C# State Machine
a4-1.description: Every async C# method becomes a hidden state machine. Learn the states a Task moves through, and how the compiler moves your method's locals to the heap.

a4-2.title: SynchronizationContext and ConfigureAwait in C#
a4-2.description: Where does your code resume after await? Learn SynchronizationContext, ConfigureAwait(false), and the classic deadlock they explain.

a4-3.title: The .NET ThreadPool Explained: Worker Threads and IOCP
a4-3.description: How the .NET ThreadPool runs your async code: worker threads, I/O completion ports and how the pool grows, which explains slowdowns under load.

a4-4.title: ValueTask vs Task in C#: When to Use ValueTask
a4-4.description: ValueTask<T> can return a result without a heap allocation. Learn when it is worth using over Task<T> in C#, and the one rule you must never break.

a4-5.title: Cancellation in .NET in Depth: Tokens, Callbacks and Linking
a4-5.description: Go beyond basic CancellationToken use: how cancellation callbacks are registered and fired, and the richer toolkit .NET builds on the same mechanism.

a4-6.title: Parallel Programming in C#: The Task Parallel Library
a4-6.description: async frees threads, while parallel code uses many cores at once. Learn the Task Parallel Library in C#, how work is partitioned, and when parallelism helps.

a4-7.title: Parallel.ForEach in C#: Process Collections in Parallel
a4-7.description: Use Parallel.ForEach to split a collection across CPU cores in C#. Learn partitioning, how to control the degree of parallelism, and its thread-safety rules.

a4-8.title: System.Threading.Channels in C#: Producer/Consumer Queues
a4-8.description: Channel<T> connects producers and consumers in .NET. Learn bounded vs unbounded channels, and how backpressure stops a fast producer overwhelming you.

a4-9.title: Concurrent Collections in C#: ConcurrentDictionary and More
a4-9.description: Share collections safely between threads with System.Collections.Concurrent: ConcurrentDictionary and the other concurrent types, and their caveats.

a4-10.title: C# lock, SemaphoreSlim and Interlocked Explained
a4-10.description: Protect shared state in C# with the right tool: what lock compiles to, SemaphoreSlim for async code, and Interlocked for atomic single-variable updates.

a4-11.title: Race Conditions in C#: Why count++ Isn't Thread-Safe
a4-11.description: A race condition gives different answers from the same input. Learn why count++ is several steps, how races happen in C#, and the two ways to prevent them.

a4-12.title: Deadlocks in C#: Lock Ordering and Async Deadlocks
a4-12.description: How deadlocks happen in C#: the classic two-lock ordering deadlock and the async deadlock, plus the discipline that prevents both of them.

a4-13.title: Thread-Safe Design in C#: Strategies Beyond Locking
a4-13.description: The best synchronization code is the code you never write. Learn a hierarchy of thread-safe design strategies in C#, strongest first, with real examples.

a4-14.title: Combining Async Streams in C# With Channels
a4-14.description: await foreach is sequential. Learn to merge several IAsyncEnumerable<T> streams in C# using a Channel as a fan-in point, with cancellation throughout.

a4-15.title: High-Throughput Async in .NET: Principles That Scale
a4-15.description: Put async and concurrency together for high throughput in .NET: avoid thread pool starvation, bound channels for backpressure, and choose Task vs ValueTask.

a5-1.title: Span<T> in C#: Slice Memory Without Copying
a5-1.description: Span<T> is a window onto memory you already own. Learn to slice arrays and buffers in C# without copying, and how a Span<T> differs from an array.

a5-2.title: ReadOnlySpan<T> and Strings: Allocation-Free Parsing in C#
a5-2.description: Use ReadOnlySpan<char> to parse and slice strings in C# without allocating substrings. A naive parser and a span-based parser compared side by side.

a5-3.title: Memory<T> vs Span<T> in C#: When You Need Memory<T>
a5-3.description: Memory<T> keeps most of Span<T>'s benefits but can be stored in fields and used across await. Learn when you need it, with a Stream.ReadAsync example.

a5-4.title: ArrayPool<T> in C#: Reuse Buffers and Cut Allocations
a5-4.description: Rent and return buffers with ArrayPool<T> in .NET instead of allocating new arrays. Learn the safe pattern, and why Rent can hand you a bigger array.

a5-5.title: MemoryPool<T> in .NET: Pooling Memory Beyond Arrays
a5-5.description: MemoryPool<T> applies pooling to Memory<T> when the memory isn't a plain array. Learn how it compares with ArrayPool<T> and when to choose it.

a5-6.title: C# ref, in and out Parameters Explained Precisely
a5-6.description: The exact rules behind C# ref, in and out: definite assignment for out, two-way references with ref, and read-only references with in.

a5-7.title: C# ref struct Explained: Rules, Restrictions, Examples
a5-7.description: Why Span<T> is safe: ref struct types in C# can never reach the heap. Learn the four restrictions one at a time, and write your own ref struct tokenizer.

a5-8.title: stackalloc in C#: Stack Allocation With Span<T>
a5-8.description: Allocate small buffers on the stack in C# with stackalloc and Span<T>, invisible to the garbage collector. Learn safe patterns and the stack overflow risk.

a5-9.title: Zero-Allocation Programming in C#: Span, Pools, stackalloc
a5-9.description: Combine Span<T>, ArrayPool, stackalloc and ref structs to write zero-allocation C#, shown with a log-line parser before and after, and the same idea in the BCL.

a5-10.title: Benchmarking .NET Code Correctly With BenchmarkDotNet
a5-10.description: A Stopwatch around a loop measures noise. Learn to benchmark C# correctly, handling JIT warm-up and GC noise, with a complete worked example.

a5-11.title: Profiling .NET Applications: CPU and Memory Profiling
a5-11.description: Find where a .NET app really spends time and memory. Learn the two kinds of CPU profiling, allocation profiling, and .NET's own diagnostic tools.

a6-1.title: SOLID Principles in C# With Before-and-After Examples
a6-1.description: The five SOLID principles explained with C# code, before and after: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov, interface segregation and dependency inversion.

a6-2.title: Clean Code in C#: Principles for Readable, Maintainable Code
a6-2.description: Clean code principles applied to C#: small functions at one level of abstraction, names that reveal intent, and other habits that keep code easy to change.

a6-3.title: Coupling and Cohesion in C#: High Cohesion, Low Coupling
a6-3.description: What coupling and cohesion mean in C# design, why changes ripple through tightly coupled code, and how to refactor toward high cohesion and low coupling.

a6-4.title: Dependency Injection at Scale in .NET: The Composition Root
a6-4.description: What changes when a .NET app has hundreds of services: a disciplined composition root, and why the service locator is an anti-pattern, side by side.

a6-5.title: Design Patterns in C#: A Practical Introduction
a6-5.description: What design patterns are and why they matter in C#: the three Gang of Four categories, and how to recognise a pattern instead of memorising code.

a6-6.title: Factory Pattern in C#: Simple Factory and Factory Method
a6-6.description: Let something other than the caller decide which class gets built. Learn the factory pattern family in C# with a notification sender selection example.

a6-7.title: Strategy Pattern in C#: Swap Algorithms at Runtime
a6-7.description: The strategy pattern in C# lets you swap an algorithm without changing the code that uses it. Shown in two forms with a shipping cost calculation.

a6-8.title: Decorator Pattern in C#: Add Behavior Without Changing Code
a6-8.description: Wrap an object to add logging or retries without touching the original class. Learn the decorator pattern in C# and how to stack several decorators.

a6-9.title: Adapter Pattern in C#: Wrap Third-Party APIs Cleanly
a6-9.description: The adapter pattern in C# lets your code see a third-party library through your own interface, so you can swap providers later. Explained with examples.

a6-10.title: Observer Pattern in C#: From GoF to the event Keyword
a6-10.description: The observer pattern in C#: the classic Gang of Four shape, and how the event keyword maps onto subjects and observers in everyday .NET code.

a6-11.title: Builder Pattern in C#: When You Still Need a Builder
a6-11.description: The builder pattern in C#: the telescoping constructor problem, how modern C# already covers most cases, and when a real builder still earns its keep.

a6-12.title: Mediator Pattern in C#: Decouple Components With a Hub
a6-12.description: The mediator pattern in C# routes communication through one object instead of many direct links, shown with a checkout dialog and request handlers.

a6-13.title: Repository Pattern in C# With EF Core: A Practical Guide
a6-13.description: Build the repository pattern in C# on top of EF Core: what belongs inside a repository and what doesn't, with the trade-offs stated honestly.

a6-14.title: Unit of Work Pattern in C# and EF Core
a6-14.description: The unit of work pattern groups changes into one commit. Learn why EF Core's DbContext already is one, and where a hand-rolled unit of work still helps.

a6-15.title: Clean Architecture in .NET: Layers and the Dependency Rule
a6-15.description: Clean Architecture in .NET explained: the four rings, the dependency rule, and one product feature flowing through the domain, application and infrastructure.

a6-16.title: Hexagonal Architecture in .NET: Ports and Adapters
a6-16.description: Hexagonal architecture, also called ports and adapters, explained for .NET developers: the same dependency rule as Clean Architecture, drawn as a hexagon.

a6-17.title: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) in C#: Core Concepts Explained
a6-17.description: The core ideas of Domain-Driven Design for C# developers, starting from ubiquitous language, explained in plain English with code examples.

a7-1.title: ASP.NET Core Architecture: Host, Kestrel and the Pipeline
a7-1.description: How ASP.NET Core is put together: the host, dependency injection and configuration you already know, plus the Kestrel web server and routing.

a7-2.title: ASP.NET Core Middleware Explained: The Request Pipeline
a7-2.description: Every ASP.NET Core request flows through a middleware pipeline and back out again. Learn why the order matters and how to write your own middleware.

a7-3.title: ASP.NET Core Filters: Action Filters and Endpoint Filters
a7-3.description: Filters run around one action, not every request. Learn ASP.NET Core action filters, how they differ from middleware, and IEndpointFilter for minimal APIs.

a7-4.title: ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs Tutorial: Routes as Functions
a7-4.description: Build HTTP APIs in ASP.NET Core with minimal APIs: map routes to functions with very little ceremony, on the same framework that runs controllers.

a7-5.title: ASP.NET Core Controllers and [ApiController] Explained
a7-5.description: Build structured APIs with ASP.NET Core controllers: routing conventions, what the [ApiController] attribute does, and when controllers beat minimal APIs.

a7-6.title: ASP.NET Core Model Binding: Route, Query, Header and Body
a7-6.description: How ASP.NET Core model binding finds request values in the route, query string, headers and body, and how to tell it exactly where to look.

a7-7.title: ASP.NET Core Validation: Data Annotations and FluentValidation
a7-7.description: Validate every incoming request in ASP.NET Core with data annotation attributes, and use FluentValidation when a rule depends on more than one property.

a7-8.title: ASP.NET Core Authentication Explained for Beginners
a7-8.description: Authentication answers one question: who is making this request? Learn how authentication works in ASP.NET Core and how it differs from authorization.

a7-9.title: ASP.NET Core Authorization: Roles, Claims and Policies
a7-9.description: Decide what an authenticated user may do in ASP.NET Core: role-based checks, claims and policy-based authorization with [Authorize], explained with examples.

a7-10.title: JWT Authentication in ASP.NET Core: How JSON Web Tokens Work
a7-10.description: How JWTs work in ASP.NET Core: header, payload and signature, why a signed token is readable by anyone, and how to validate bearer tokens correctly.

a7-11.title: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect Explained for .NET Developers
a7-11.description: OAuth 2.0 lets an app act on your behalf without your password, and OpenID Connect adds who you are. Learn both, and how ASP.NET Core uses them.

a7-12.title: Rate Limiting in ASP.NET Core: Protect Your API
a7-12.description: Protect ASP.NET Core APIs with the built-in rate limiting middleware, and learn why limits guard against well-meaning clients as much as attackers.

a7-13.title: Caching in ASP.NET Core: IMemoryCache Explained
a7-13.description: Speed up ASP.NET Core by caching expensive results with IMemoryCache. Learn expiration, what to cache, and why cache invalidation is famously hard.

a7-14.title: Distributed Caching in ASP.NET Core With IDistributedCache
a7-14.description: Why IMemoryCache breaks when you run several instances, and how IDistributedCache gives every ASP.NET Core server one shared cache.

a7-15.title: Resilience in .NET: Retries, Timeouts and Circuit Breakers
a7-15.description: Handle failing dependencies in .NET deliberately: retries with backoff, timeouts and circuit breakers, and how naive retries cause a thundering herd.

a7-16.title: Health Checks in ASP.NET Core: Liveness and Readiness
a7-16.description: Add health check endpoints to ASP.NET Core so orchestrators know when your app is broken. Learn liveness vs readiness, and why one endpoint isn't enough.

a7-17.title: Observability in .NET: Logs, Metrics and Traces Explained
a7-17.description: The three pillars of observability for .NET apps: logs, metrics and distributed traces, what each one can't show alone, and how they work together.

a7-18.title: OpenTelemetry in .NET: Traces, Metrics and Logs Setup
a7-18.description: Instrument .NET apps once with OpenTelemetry and export to any backend. Learn how OTel builds on .NET's existing primitives, plus auto-instrumentation.

a8-1.title: Advanced EF Core: Global Query Filters and More
a8-1.description: EF Core at production depth: global query filters and other advanced mechanisms for querying and saving data fast, safely and correctly at scale.

a8-2.title: EF Core Query Optimization: Split Queries Explained
a8-2.description: Make correct EF Core queries fast: why including two collections multiplies rows, how split queries fix it, and how to shape exactly what you load.

a8-3.title: EF Core Compiled Queries: When They Actually Help
a8-3.description: EF Core already caches query shapes. Learn what compiled queries actually save, and the narrow cases where using them is genuinely worth it.

a8-4.title: EF Core Transactions and Isolation Levels Explained
a8-4.description: Go beyond BeginTransaction and Commit in EF Core: SQL isolation levels, what each one lets other transactions see, and transactions across several saves.

a8-5.title: EF Core Concurrency Conflicts: Resolution Strategies
a8-5.description: Catching DbUpdateConcurrencyException is the easy part. Learn the strategies for resolving EF Core concurrency conflicts, with code for each one.

a8-6.title: EF Core Connection Management and Pool Sizing
a8-6.description: A scoped DbContext doesn't hold one database connection open per request. Learn how EF Core really opens connections, and how to size the pool.

a8-7.title: Stored Procedures in EF Core: FromSql and ExecuteSql Safely
a8-7.description: Call stored procedures from EF Core safely, and learn which raw SQL methods parameterize your values for you and which ones invite SQL injection.

a8-8.title: EF Core Bulk Operations: ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete
a8-8.description: Update or delete thousands of rows in one SQL statement with EF Core's ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete, skipping change tracking. Trade-offs explained.

a8-9.title: EF Core Caching Strategies: Identity Map and Beyond
a8-9.description: The caching layers in an EF Core app: the DbContext identity map, IMemoryCache and distributed caches, and the invalidation rules each one needs.

a8-10.title: Raw SQL vs EF Core: When to Use Each in .NET
a8-10.description: EF Core or raw SQL? Why both absolute positions are wrong, where EF Core's generated SQL is fine, and when hand-written SQL genuinely wins.

a8-11.title: Troubleshooting Slow Database Queries in .NET and EF Core
a8-11.description: Diagnose a slow database in .NET instead of guessing: make the SQL and its timings visible first, then fix the real cause with the right tool.

a9-1.title: REST API Design Best Practices: The Richardson Maturity Model
a9-1.description: Design REST APIs other teams can rely on: the Richardson Maturity Model, resource design, and keeping a contract stable when other services depend on it.

a9-2.title: Microservices in .NET: Benefits, Costs and Boundaries
a9-2.description: Microservices move complexity from your code to the network. Learn when that trade is worth it, where service boundaries come from, and what it costs.

a9-3.title: Message-Based Architecture: Asynchronous Messaging in .NET
a9-3.description: Decouple services in time with messages instead of synchronous calls. Learn message-based architecture and why it reshapes everything downstream.

a9-4.title: Message Queues Explained: Competing Consumers in .NET
a9-4.description: How message queues distribute work: durable storage, explicit acknowledgement, and competing consumers where only one listener ever gets each message.

a9-5.title: Apache Kafka Fundamentals for .NET Developers
a9-5.description: Kafka is not a queue but a distributed, replicated log. Learn how it retains events and lets many independent readers replay them at their own pace.

a9-6.title: Event-Driven Architecture in .NET: Events Across Services
a9-6.description: Event-driven architecture takes in-process C# events across the network. Learn how services publish facts, how others react, and how to name events.

a9-7.title: Idempotency in Distributed Systems: Idempotency Keys in .NET
a9-7.description: At-least-once delivery means duplicates will happen. Learn how duplicates arise and two techniques to make operations idempotent, including idempotency keys.

a9-8.title: Message Retries and Dead-Letter Queues Explained
a9-8.description: Retry failed message handling safely: bounded retries, delivery counts and dead-letter queues, and why retries without idempotency cause harm.

a9-9.title: Circuit Breaker Pattern in .NET: Closed, Open, Half-Open
a9-9.description: Stop cascading failures with the circuit breaker pattern: the closed, open and half-open states explained precisely, and how it protects .NET services.

a9-10.title: Distributed Transactions and Two-Phase Commit Explained
a9-10.description: Why ACID across independent services is hard, how two-phase commit works, and why it falls short for the distributed .NET systems built today.

a9-11.title: Outbox Pattern in .NET: Reliable Event Publishing
a9-11.description: Writing to the database and publishing an event can't be atomic. The transactional outbox pattern makes it one step. Learn how it works in .NET.

a9-12.title: Eventual Consistency and the CAP Theorem Explained
a9-12.description: Why distributed systems can't always show the latest write instantly, what the CAP theorem says, and how to engineer around the consistency window.

a10-1.title: Cloud Configuration in .NET: Twelve-Factor Config
a10-1.description: How .NET configuration changes in the cloud: no server to edit, config injected fresh on every start, and the twelve-factor app approach to settings.

a10-2.title: Docker for .NET Developers: Multi-Stage Dockerfile Guide
a10-2.description: Containerize .NET apps with Docker: what a container really is, and how a multi-stage Dockerfile builds a small, production-ready image.

a10-3.title: Containerize ASP.NET Core: Ports, Binding and Docker
a10-3.description: Why an ASP.NET Core app that works locally refuses traffic inside a container, how to bind to all interfaces, and how to build a container-ready app.

a10-4.title: Environment Variables in .NET: The Double Underscore Rule
a10-4.description: Map environment variables to nested .NET configuration keys with the double underscore convention, so container and cloud settings bind correctly.

a10-5.title: Secrets Management in .NET: Keeping Credentials Safe
a10-5.description: Secrets need a higher bar than ordinary configuration. Learn why, and how .NET apps load credentials from dedicated secret stores instead of config files.

a10-6.title: Kubernetes Health Probes for .NET: Liveness vs Readiness
a10-6.description: How Kubernetes calls your .NET health endpoints: liveness and readiness probes, httpGet probe configuration, and what happens when a probe fails.

a10-7.title: Logging in Containers: Structured Logs From .NET Apps
a10-7.description: Containers have no log files you can tail. Learn how .NET apps should write structured logs in a container and let the platform collect and keep them.

a10-8.title: Scaling .NET Apps Horizontally: Why Statelessness Matters
a10-8.description: Vertical scaling hits a ceiling. Learn horizontal, elastic scaling for .NET apps, and why statelessness is what lets you run twenty instances safely.

a10-9.title: Cloud-Native .NET: Designing Apps for the Cloud
a10-9.description: Running in the cloud is not the same as being cloud-native. Learn the design principles that let .NET apps expect failure and scale with the platform.

a10-10.title: .NET Aspire Tutorial: Introduction to the AppHost
a10-10.description: Get started with .NET Aspire: describe your app's services and dependencies in code with an AppHost project, with orchestration and telemetry built in.

a11-1.title: Unit Testing in C# With xUnit: A Practical Guide
a11-1.description: Write unit tests in C# with xUnit, and see how automated tests replace manual checking as your .NET code grows. Clear examples from the first test up.

a11-2.title: Integration Testing in ASP.NET Core: Test the Real App
a11-2.description: Test the real, assembled ASP.NET Core application and catch the wiring and configuration bugs that unit tests can never see.

a11-3.title: Mocking in C# With Moq: Mocks vs Stubs Explained
a11-3.description: Isolate code under test in C# with Moq. Learn the precise difference between mocks and stubs, and how depending on abstractions makes mocking possible.

a11-4.title: Testcontainers in .NET: Test Against a Real Database
a11-4.description: Use Testcontainers in .NET to start a real database in Docker for your tests, instead of mocks or in-memory providers that hide real bugs.

a11-5.title: API Testing in .NET: Test the Contract, Not Just the Logic
a11-5.description: Correct logic doesn't guarantee a correct API. Learn to test status codes, headers and JSON field names in .NET so contract breaks are caught early.

a11-6.title: Performance Testing .NET APIs: Percentiles, Not Averages
a11-6.description: Measure .NET API performance the right way: define a target, generate realistic load, and read latency percentiles instead of misleading averages.

a11-7.title: Load Testing .NET Applications: Find Your Breaking Point
a11-7.description: Load test .NET apps to find where they break before your users do: the three common shapes of load test and how to read what they tell you.

a11-8.title: Debugging .NET in Production: Observe Without Pausing
a11-8.description: You can't pause production. Learn how to debug live .NET apps by observing without stopping them and capturing evidence for later analysis.

a11-9.title: Finding Memory Leaks in .NET Applications
a11-9.description: .NET has a GC but can still leak. Learn the few patterns behind most leaks, especially event handlers, and how to follow a GC root chain to the cause.

a11-10.title: Diagnosing High CPU in .NET Apps: A Practical Guide
a11-10.description: Tell healthy load from a bug when CPU hits 100%. Learn the usual suspects, a step-by-step diagnosis flow, and a real catastrophic regex backtracking case.

a11-11.title: Diagnosing Deadlocks in Production .NET Apps
a11-11.description: Find a deadlock in a .NET process you can't step through: freeze the whole picture, read the threads, and tell a deadlock from thread pool starvation.

a11-12.title: Thread Pool Starvation in .NET: Causes and Fixes
a11-12.description: Every request hangs, but nothing is deadlocked. Learn why the .NET thread pool grows slowly on purpose, how starvation happens, and how to fix it.

a11-13.title: Database Bottlenecks in .NET: Diagnose Slow Data Access
a11-13.description: When a .NET app is slow because of its database: the recurring root causes, a diagnosis flow, and worked examples starting with N+1 queries.

a11-14.title: Production Incident Analysis for .NET Applications
a11-14.description: Five failure modes can look identical in production. Learn a diagnostic decision tree for .NET incidents that rules causes out instead of guessing.

a12-1.title: What's New in C# 14: Every New Feature Explained
a12-1.description: A guided tour of C# 14: extension members, the field keyword, null-conditional assignment, span conversions, partial constructors and more, with examples.

a12-2.title: C# 14 Extension Members: Extension Properties Explained
a12-2.description: C# 14 extension members in full: extension properties, static extension members and the extension block syntax, and what it means for extension methods.

a12-3.title: C# 14 field Keyword: Field-Backed Properties Explained
a12-3.description: C# 14's field keyword lets a property add logic without declaring its own backing field. Compare auto-properties, full properties and the new style.

a12-4.title: C# 14 Null-Conditional Assignment: ?. on the Left Side
a12-4.description: C# 14 lets ?. and ?[] appear on the left of an assignment, so the value is only assigned when the object isn't null. The rules, with examples.

a12-5.title: C# 14 Span Conversions: Implicit Span<T> Conversions
a12-5.description: C# 14 adds implicit conversions between arrays, Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<T>, making span-based APIs easier to call. What changed and why it matters.

a12-6.title: C# 14 Lambda Parameter Modifiers Without Types
a12-6.description: In C# 14, lambda parameters can use modifiers like ref and out without spelling out their types. See the before and after, and the rules.

a12-7.title: C# 14 Partial Constructors Explained
a12-7.description: C# 14 lets a constructor be split into a declaring part and an implementing part, so a source generator can supply the body. How it works, with examples.

a12-8.title: C# 14 User-Defined Compound Assignment Operators
a12-8.description: C# 14 lets a type define += and other compound assignment operators directly, so a += b can update in place instead of creating a new value.

a12-9.title: C# File-Based Apps: Run a Single .cs File With dotnet run
a12-9.description: Run a C# program from a single .cs file with dotnet run, with no project file needed. Learn how file-based apps work in .NET 10 and when to use them.

a13-1.title: Designing an Enterprise .NET Application: Capstone Blueprint
a13-1.description: Start the capstone: design OrderFlow, an order-management system in .NET, from its core entities and services to the constraints it must handle.

a13-2.title: Clean Architecture Project in .NET: OrderFlow Capstone
a13-2.description: Apply Clean Architecture to a real .NET order-management API: what lives in each project, and how placing an order flows through all four layers.

a13-3.title: Authorization Policies in a Real ASP.NET Core API
a13-3.description: Decide endpoint by endpoint what users may do in OrderFlow, the ASP.NET Core capstone API, with real authorization policies and resource checks.

a13-4.title: EF Core in a Real Project: Repository and Pooling
a13-4.description: Wire EF Core into the OrderFlow capstone: a real repository, query optimization and connection pool sizing working together in one .NET API.

a13-5.title: Redis Caching in a Real .NET API: Cache-Aside Pattern
a13-5.description: Add Redis to the OrderFlow capstone with the cache-aside pattern, and trace a price change end to end to keep cached data correct across instances.

a13-6.title: Background Processing Pipeline With BackgroundService
a13-6.description: Run OrderFlow's checkout pipeline with .NET's BackgroundService: one base class, four stages, and an honest look at what this design can't survive.

a13-7.title: Reliable Messaging With Kafka and the Outbox Pattern
a13-7.description: Close OrderFlow's reliability gap with the outbox pattern published through Kafka, so checkout events survive crashes and reach every consumer.

a13-8.title: Structured Logging Across Services: Correlated .NET Logs
a13-8.description: Make one order's journey through five services readable: correlated, structured logging in a real .NET system, stage by stage through the pipeline.

a13-9.title: Monitoring a .NET System With Business Metrics
a13-9.description: Go beyond auto-instrumentation: add the business metrics that tell you whether OrderFlow is healthy right now, before any customer notices a problem.

a13-10.title: Choosing a Testing Strategy for a Real .NET Application
a13-10.description: Match each testing technique to what each part of OrderFlow actually risks, instead of applying one kind of test everywhere in the codebase.

a13-11.title: Containerizing a Real .NET App: Docker Image and Probes
a13-11.description: Ship OrderFlow as a container image a cluster can run, restart and health-check, with one readiness endpoint covering its three real dependencies.

a13-12.title: Performance Optimization in .NET: Profile, Fix, Verify
a13-12.description: Turn a slow spot on the OrderFlow dashboard into a profiled, fixed and verified improvement, starting with N+1 queries hidden in the hot path.

a13-13.title: Production Deployment Pipeline for a .NET Application
a13-13.description: Take OrderFlow from a laptop to production with a deployment pipeline that enforces what each stage must prove before customers get the release.

a13-14.title: .NET Architecture Review: Capstone Wrap-Up
a13-14.description: A final architecture review of the OrderFlow capstone: step back from thirteen working pieces and check the whole distributed .NET system holds together.
